note: Recast from the description of the new species by Rocha & Cancello (2009), original in English; the original records the alate as Unknown; no measurement data.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier differs from all other species of the genus in the apex of the left mandible forming a distinct hook-like bend and the apex of the right mandible forming an angle of 90º with the base of the mandible.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Sides of the head slightly convergent anteriorly in dorsal view. Dorsal tubercle slightly prominent in lateral view, situated behind the lateral projection. Mandibles type 2, the apex of the left mandible strongly bent into a distinct apical hook, the apex of the right mandible forming an angle of 90º with the proximal part of the mandible, which bears a tooth-like process on the proximal half. Head capsule sparsely setose and with short hairs, denser ventrally, minute hairs scattered over the whole head capsule and denser in the apical region. Postmentum with setae. Surface of the pronotum with short hairs and the margins with setae; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum with setae; abdominal tergites and sternites densely setose, the posterior margin with erect setae.
